That one's the plain constant (safe). Here's the full picture:

## Callers of `truncate_and_trailoff` (`crates/util/src/util.rs:58`)

The function has `debug_assert!(max_chars >= 5)`, so the only real risk across all callers is whether `max_chars` can dip below 5 (panic in debug/test builds; in release it just silently returns a near-empty/`"…"` string).

**High confidence — `max_chars` is a hardcoded constant ≥ 5, no arithmetic on it:**
- `activity_indicator.rs:668` — `MAX_MESSAGE_LEN` (50)
- `debugger_ui/dropdown_menus.rs:35,83,315` — `MAX_LABEL_CHARS` (150 / 50 / 150)
- `agent_ui/conversation_view/thread_view.rs:1461` — literal `200`
- `terminal.rs:2162,2195,2196` — `MAX_CHARS` (25)
- `search/project_search.rs:661` — `MAX_TAB_TITLE_LEN` (24, from `editor`)
- `title_bar.rs:730,878` — `MAX_PROJECT_NAME_LENGTH` / `MAX_BRANCH_NAME_LENGTH` (40)
- `tasks_ui/modal.rs:529` — `MAX_TAGS_LINE_LEN` (30)
- `editor/items.rs:770,784` — `MAX_TAB_TITLE_LEN` (24)
- `agent/tools/update_title_tool.rs:96` — `MAX_TITLE_LEN` (200)
- `git_ui/blame_ui.rs:44` — `GIT_BLAME_MAX_AUTHOR_CHARS_DISPLAYED` (20)
- `git_ui/commit_view.rs:935` — literal `20` (the `.split('\n').next().unwrap()` next to it is also safe — `split` always yields ≥1 item)
- `git_ui/picker_prompt.rs:220` — `max_match_length`, traced to its only construction site (`picker_prompt.rs:39`, `prompt()` helper), which always passes literal `70`. All three call sites in `git_panel.rs` go through that helper, so this is effectively constant too.

**Lower confidence — derived value, could plausibly drop below 5:**
- `activity_indicator.rs:579-582` — `MAX_MESSAGE_LEN.saturating_sub(health_str.len())`, where `health_str` is `format!("({server_name}) Warning: ")` (or `Error:`/plain). If `server_name` is long enough (roughly >33 chars for the "Warning" case), the resulting `max_chars` falls under 5, which would trip the `debug_assert` in debug/test builds (and produce a near-empty truncated string in release). This is the one caller I'd flag as worth a bounds check or a `.max(5)` clamp, since language server names aren't bounded in length.
